facts.statement: The genus Asiahesperornis was described by Nesov and Prizemlin in 1991.
Asiahesperornis is a genus of flightless, toothed birds that swam by moving their feet.
facts.quote: Asiahesperornis is a prehistoric foot-propelled diving toothed flightless bird genus from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous along the shores of the ancient Turgai Sea in what is now Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: It lived in what today is Kazakhstan, at its time the shores of the shallow Turgai Sea.

facts.statement: Asiahesperornis belongs to the group Hesperornithes, which consisted of flightless, toothed seabirds from the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: It was a member of the Hesperornithes, flightless toothed seabirds of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: While its exact placement is debated, Asiahesperornis is likely a member of the family Hesperornithidae.
facts.quote: Its exact relationships are not completely resolved, but it probably belongs into the Hesperornithidae just like Hesperornis

facts.statement: Fossils of Asiahesperornis date from the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Asiahesperornis is classified within the family Hesperornithidae.
In the Paleobiology Database, Asiahesperornis is classified under the class Reptilia.
